en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Chapter on Leaning on a Support, 21.
The Training Rule on Leaning on a Support.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks walked through inhabited areas with their hands on their hips...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not walk through an inhabited area with my hands on my hips.
One must not walk through an inhabited area with one's hands on one's hips.

If, out of disrespect, one walks between houses with hands on hips, whether on one side or both, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa). There is no offense if it is unintentional … [and so forth] …
thus ends the first training rule.
